system.summary: Villeroy-office cipher: letters as figures and letter-shaped symbols with homophones, marked letters (comma, one or two dots) for words in alphabetical series, two-digit figures for names and syllables.

diacritics.note: Comma, one dot or two dots on a letter select a word series (f, = le; x, = que; t: = de).

system.doubled_letters: special sign (phi doubles the preceding symbol)
system.sibling_key: Bazeries 1901 prints the 1599 key given to Bethune's brother, same office and design, other values; used for the design only.
system.notes: Known names and words: 48 Cardinal, 17 Aldobrandin, 7 le Roy d'Espagne, 6 (standalone) Sa Saintete; 61 qui, 63 re, 65 si, 66 sa, 68 tout, 71 tion, 72 vous, 73 vostre. 72, 6 and 66 fixed on 14 Nov 2026 from the f. 53r gloss.

prior_solution.where: Halphen 1889 prints the 9 Nov (f. 33) and 22 Nov (f. 46) letters in clear from the originals; clear minute f. 36 for 10 Nov; marginal glosses of other letters

solution.what: Volume fetched from Gallica; leaves mapped; the clear minute of 10 Nov found at f. 36 by reading the sheets.
EM alignment of the 10 Nov cipher with its minute plus the glossed passages of 8 Nov and 10 Dec gives the letter values and word signs.
10 Nov letter read in full against the minute.
9 Nov letter decoded with the key and language-model decoders: about six words in ten.
4x re-transcription fixed the doubling sign and the syllable groups 61-73.
Oracle on the known-plaintext blocks: transcription caps decoding at about 71 % of letters; decoder already at the ceiling.
Automatic glyph segmentation and template alignment.
22 Nov letter transcribed in full; clear text read, cipher runs decode to fragments only.
Full-resolution re-reading and figure-split lattice on f. 33; union of two independent readings worth about 2.9 points.
Xivrey, Melanges de Colbert 17, fr. 3677/3678 excluded; Cinq cents de Colbert 346 and Halphen's edition identified, not accessible.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1107 tokens, 100 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.627 per letter; polyphonic: 33% of read tokens differ from their type's commonest value. Verdict: not applicable.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): 10 Nov corpus_v2.txt + reading_10nov.md; 9 Nov ct_f33_v2.txt + decoder output decode_f33_v3/v2 (substance only); 22 Nov reading_22nov.md + ct_22nov.txt (cipher runs decoded only in fragments); key key.tsv

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test): reading_10nov.md reads (83% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py, from the clear minute); decode_f33_v3.txt (9 Nov) gives broken lines with nonsense words, and the 22 Nov cipher runs are fragments ('a substance, not a reading'). 9 Nov and 22 Nov relabelled decoded, not read; fraction_read 0.55 -> ~0.2 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b17), step 1: Halphen, Lettres inedites du roi Henri IV a monsieur de Bethune ... du 18 octobre au 24 decembre 1601 (1889) found in full view on HathiTrust (record 100644113, item iau.31858014633857, public domain); babel.hathitrust.org answers with a Cloudflare human-verification page (curl 403; the browser pane shows the checkbox), which this session does not pass. Not on the Internet Archive, Gallica or Google Books (searched). Not on DECODE.

Re-read, step 2: no new image route or transcription; the measured transcription ceiling (oracle 71%, two readers agree on 69% of glyphs, third pass) stands, so the 9 Nov and 22 Nov decodes stay fragments. Both kept decoded, not read; the edition is the route.

Consistency pass (cl): 'read in part' not justified: the Halphen 1889 gap is genuinely untried (not-attempted kept) and the print, key-rebuild and retry escalation steps are not done (left unticked); NOTES Status: in progress. The umbrella gap line for the 9 and 22 Nov runs restated as a lead sentence (its two letters are separate gap lines, mirrored in outcome.gaps).

Verification pass (Claude Opus 5.5): the eight cipher lines of f. 53r block 1 transcribed and aligned with their verbatim marginal gloss (f53r_alignment.md): 72 = vous (four aligned occurrences; settles the earlier proposal and the D1 counter-indication), standalone 6 = Sa Saintete (three), 66 = sa (one), plus 3: = faire, +. = de, n, = nous. Pre-registered check (SHA-256 285ddb07...) on glossed blocks not used for the derivation (f. 56r, f. 50r): one locatable occurrence, agrees; not conclusive; the 200-shuffled-key measurement is not applicable to groups this rare. Three 22 Nov runs give sense (vostre negotiation; correspondance ... discretion; le respect), probable only. Halphen 1889 still behind HathiTrust's human check (403). 9 and 22 Nov stay decoded, not read.

Halphen 1889 (HathiTrust iau.31858014633857) opened by a person in a browser, pp. 8-34: prints the 9 Nov letters (f. 30, f. 33), 10 Nov (f. 34), 18 Nov (f. 38) and 22 Nov (f. 46, from p. 33) from the originals, the ciphered passages given in clear and not marked. Halphen dates the glossed letter ff. 30-31 to 9 Nov (NOTES leaf map: 8 Nov).

One pre-registered measurement (PREREG SHA-256 2e3d1707..., script ce5daf65...): frozen key (first value per symbol, no LM) on the whole f. 33 run (970 tokens, ct_f33_v2.txt) against Halphen's clear (1,460 letters), 1 - Levenshtein/max length: 0.507; 200 shuffled keys best 0.291, mean 0.251. Default bar (>= 0.85 and >= best + 0.30) not met; key-signal bar (>= best + 0.15) met. Word classes of the printed text against the decode: 130 sure, 105 probable, 118 restored of 353.

Clear frames of Halphen's text aligned with the decoded runs of f. 33 and f. 46r: 12 = le Grand Duc, 20 = la Seigneurie de Venise, 28 = Espagne, 26 = France, 27 = Italie, 44 = Prince(s), 45 = Duc, 70 = partant; 69 tous?, 67 sans? (halphen_check.md, key.tsv).

Second pre-registered measurement on a fresh portion (PREREG SHA-256 5ad234e5..., key K' = f. 33 key + 12, 20, 26, 27, 28, 44, 45, 67, 69, 70): 34 chunks, 1,062 tokens of ff. 46v-47v and f. 46r l. 31, segmented from the clear frames before decoding, against Halphen pp. 34-40: 0.535; 200 shuffled keys best 0.319, mean 0.276. Default bar not met, key-signal bar met. Strict count on the 371 printed words: 136 sure, 107 probable, 128 restored. (One accidental re-run through an import, fixed seed, same figures.)

outcome.method_basis: The 9 and 22 Nov 1601 letters are printed in clear from the originals by Halphen (1889), pp. 16-18 and 33-40; the 10 Nov letter reads from its clear minute f. 36. The key rebuilt from the minute and the glosses (EM alignment, 17 Sept 2026; f. 53r gloss and Halphen alignments, 14 Nov 2026) decodes both printed letters well above shuffled keys (0.507 and 0.535 against best controls 0.291 and 0.319).
outcome.fraction_read_source: 14 Nov 2026: every cipher token of the three letters has a clear text (minute f. 36 for 10 Nov; Halphen 1889 for 9 and 22 Nov). The cipher alone supports about two thirds of the printed words (9 Nov 235/353, 22 Nov fresh part 243/371, sure + probable), so the reading rests on the print, not on the decode.
outcome.notes: Read from an existing decipherment: 10 Nov from the minute f. 36, 9 and 22 Nov from Halphen 1889 (pp. 16-18, 33-40). Two pre-registered measurements of the frozen key against Halphen (f. 33: 0.507 vs best control 0.291; ff. 46v-47v: 0.535 vs 0.319) miss the 0.85 bar but show the key carries the printed text. Code groups: 6, 66, 72 from the f. 53r gloss; 12, 20, 26, 27, 28, 44, 45, 70 from Halphen; open 2, 3, 5, 8, 9, 31, 62, 80 (codes_open counts these 8).

texts.label: 10 Nov 1601, f. 34r-v
texts.summary: Henri IV tells Béthune that he paid Cardinal Aldobrandini 10,000 écus through Sillery as a gratification after the Parlement's judgment in the Este-Aldobrandini debt, and will pay 10,000 more in the first months of 1602; Béthune is to tell the Cardinal through Cardinal d'Ossat and pretend not to have received the letter. The cipher is entries A to V3 of corpus_v2.txt (the other entries are glossed passages of the 8 Nov and 10 Dec letters); the text comes from the clear minute on f. 36.

reading_review.note: The four cipher passages read from the clear minute f. 36r-v, which gives their full text; continuous French.

texts.note: Read from an existing decipherment: Halphen 1889 pp. 16-18 prints the whole ciphered passage in clear (not reproduced here; HathiTrust copy). The frozen key decodes f. 33 to 0.507 similarity with his text (best of 200 shuffled keys 0.291); 130 of his 353 words are confirmed letter by letter, 105 in part, 118 restored from the print (halphen_check.md).
texts.label: 9 Nov 1601, f. 33r
texts.summary: Henri IV reports, from La Rochepot's secretary in Spain, that the King of Spain has taken the Duke of Modena and the Princes of la Mirandola under his protection with pensions on the revenue of Naples and the Golden Fleece; Bethune is to confer with Cardinal Aldobrandini, the King drops the idea of courting Cardinal d'Este, and the cardinals of Joyeuse and d'Ossat are to advise on Don Alessandro's promotion. Text: Halphen 1889, pp. 16-18.

reading_review.note: Text from the printed edition, checked against the cipher by one pre-registered measurement and a word-level alignment; the text itself is not in the repository.

texts.note: Read from an existing decipherment: Halphen 1889 pp. 33-40 prints the whole letter with the ciphered passages in clear (not reproduced here; HathiTrust copy). Fresh-portion measurement of the frozen key K' on ff. 46v-47v: 0.535 against best of 200 shuffled keys 0.319; on the 371 printed words of the measured runs, 136 confirmed letter by letter, 107 in part, 128 restored from the print. reading_22nov.md's clear transcription has errors to correct against Halphen (halphen_check.md).
texts.label: 22 Nov 1601, ff. 46r-47v
texts.summary: Henri IV answers Bethune's despatch of 29 October: his negotiation with the Grand Duke and Grand Duchess of Tuscany; Venice and the Grand Duke should have stopped Spain's taking Modena and la Mirandola under its protection; three French candidates for the cardinalate (Evreux, the old Archbishop of Vienne, Clermont); the idea of binding Cardinal Aldobrandini to France with the protection of French affairs; Camaiano's pension; Chateau-Dauphin, Barberini, the Jesuits, the Council; the nuncio in Switzerland; a postscript preferring Clermont to Vienne. Text: Halphen 1889, pp. 33-40.

reading_review.note: Text from the printed edition, checked against the cipher by a pre-registered measurement on a fresh portion and a word-level alignment; the text itself is not in the repository.
